extracted.intended_audience: title IV-E agencies; state and tribal child welfare agencies; attorneys and legal service providers working in foster care; tribal governments; policy staff and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the regulatory standards and criteria in ACF's proposed rule (NPRM) that define when and how title IV-E agencies may claim Federal financial participation (FFP) for legal representation in foster care and related civil proceedings. Focuses on allowable costs, definitions, required documentation/conditions, and examples of covered activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable administrative cost: agency attorney representation in foster care proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representation in foster care proceedings provided by an attorney representing the title IV-E agency or any other public agency which has an agreement in effect under which the other agency has placement and care responsibility of a title IV-E eligible child pursuant to 472(a)(2)(B)(ii) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specified as a separate example of allowable administrative costs and is intended to encompass public agencies and tribes that have an agreement under section 472(a)(2)(B)(ii). It is not a new concept but is clarified as an explicit example in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable administrative cost: independent legal representation for eligible child, parent, relative caregiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent legal representation provided by an attorney representing a child in title IV-E foster care, a child who is a candidate for title IV-E foster care, the child's parent(s), and the child's relative caregiver in foster care and other civil legal proceedings as necessary to carry out the requirements in the agency's title IV-E foster care plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent representation in civil proceedings may include facilitating, arranging, brokering, advocating, or otherwise linking clients with providers and services identified in the child's case plan pursuant to sections 422, 471(a)(16), and 475 of the Act. Title IV-E agencies may claim administrative costs of paralegals, investigators, peer partners, or social workers that support an attorney providing such representation to the extent necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable administrative cost: tribal attorney representation when tribe intervenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representation provided by an attorney representing an Indian child's tribe (as defined by 25 U.S.C. 1903(5)), when the child's tribe intervenes in any state court proceeding for the foster care placement or termination of parental rights of an Indian child who is in title IV-E foster care or an Indian child who is a candidate for title IV-E foster care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF proposes this because tribal representation can provide the cultural and social standards needed for courts to determine reasonable efforts and finalize permanency; it supports tribal self-governance and avoids unintended adverse consequences like loss of tribal membership and benefits. It is an allowable administrative cost when it fulfills a specific title IV-E plan requirement and is found necessary by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition of allowability: necessary to carry out agency's title IV-E foster care plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposed legal representation costs must be 'necessary to carry out the requirements in the agency's title IV-E foster care plan' in order to be allowable administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF repeatedly ties allowability to necessity for executing specific plan requirements (e.g., reasonable efforts, permanency, education stability, transition planning). The administrative cost must serve a plan requirement identified under sections such as 471(a) and 475.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standard for 'independent' legal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, such legal representation should be provided by an attorney who: does not have a concurrent conflict of interest; does not accept compensation for representing a client from someone other than the client unless the client gives informed consent; and there is no interference with the lawyer's independence of professional judgment or with the client-lawyer relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title IV-E agency may determine what 'independent' means for purposes of providing such legal representation, but ACF sets these baseline conflict/independence conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable supporting personnel costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IV-E agencies may claim title IV-E administrative costs of paralegals, investigators, peer partners or social workers that support an attorney providing independent legal representation to the extent that they are necessary to support the attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with Children's Bureau policy; such supporting staff costs are allowable only to the extent necessary and in support of the attorney's representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/coverage of 'parent(s)' and 'legal guardianship' for claiming costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under title IV-E of the Act, 'parent(s)' means a biological or adoptive parent(s) or legal guardian(s), as determined by applicable state or tribal law (section 475(2) of the Act). 'Legal guardianship' means a judicially created relationship intended to be permanent and self-sustaining as evidenced by transfer of parental rights (section 475(7) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies may claim administrative costs of independent legal representation for a legal guardian(s) of a child eligible for title IV-E foster care if state or tribal law considers the legal guardian a parent and such guardian is intended to be the permanent caretaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to define 'relative' for relative caregivers
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of claiming the cost of independent legal representation provided to the relative caregiver of a child who is eligible for title IV-E foster care, the title IV-E agency may define the term 'relative'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a title IV-E agency may define relative to include kin and 'fictive-kin'. This allows agencies to include relative caregivers even when they are not legal guardians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable civil legal representation activities (service linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent legal representation in civil legal proceedings includes facilitating, arranging, brokering, advocating, or otherwise linking clients with providers and services as identified in the child's case plan pursuant to section 475(1) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include advocating to obtain a housing voucher, appealing a denial of a voucher, or suing a landlord to address unsafe conditions to execute the child's case plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific examples of civil proceedings that may be allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys may provide independent legal representation in civil proceedings such as: establishing paternity; obtaining orders of protection for victims of family violence; enrollment in school/accessing education records; establishing a health care power of attorney or proxy; resolving inaccuracies in a youth's credit report; obtaining/changing official documentation (birth certificate, SSN, medical records, state ID); assisting youth aging out to access public benefits, housing, health insurance, and education—when necessary to meet plan requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each example is linked to a particular plan requirement or statutory citation (e.g., paternity for IV-E eligibility or for termination timelines, education stability per 471(a)(30) and 475(1)(G) and (5)(D), transition planning per 475(5)(H), documentation per 471(a)(27) and 475(5)(I)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of 'candidate' status for title IV-E
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'candidate' for title IV-E foster care is a child who is potentially eligible for title IV-E foster care maintenance payments and is at serious risk of removal as evidenced by the title IV-E agency either pursuing the child's removal from the home or making reasonable efforts to prevent such removal (section 472(i) of the Act). The agency must document the child's candidacy for title IV-E through one of the three acceptable methods identified in the Child Welfare Policy Manual (e.g., a case plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A child is not a candidate merely because described as 'at risk' absent formal agency involvement or formal indicators such as a case plan or agency pursuit of removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFP rate and claiming rules for administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency may claim Federal financial participation (FFP) at the rate of 50 percent for allowable title IV-E foster care administrative costs, including allowable legal representation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure costs are reasonable and allocated according to approved cost allocation plans; examples and estimates of Federal, non-Federal, and total costs are provided in the NPRM's fiscal tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness and cost allocation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IV-E agencies must ensure costs are reasonable (45 CFR 1335.30(i) applying 45 CFR 75.404). The title IV-E agency must describe how the administrative costs of allowable legal representation are allocated in a public assistance cost allocation plan reviewed and approved by HHS (45 CFR 1355.30(k) applying 45 CFR 95.507).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contracting with other public or private agencies, claims must be consistent with the cost allocation plan and supported by a written agreement specifying services and basis for billing (45 CFR 95.507(b)(6)). ACF requests comments on what a 'prudent person' would reasonably pay for attorney fees in civil legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional implementation by title IV-E agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the option of the title IV-E agency with placement and care responsibility of the child whether or not to implement this option to claim FFP for legal representation for the purposes described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF notes that it is optional for agencies to claim these administrative costs; agencies retain discretion whether to implement the option to claim FFP for independent or tribal legal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal representation by non-attorneys (consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACF is considering allowing the cost of a non-attorney to represent a child's tribe when it is necessary for the administration of the title IV-E plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF seeks comments and evidence that non-attorneys would effectively provide the necessary cultural/social information to courts, and recommendations for how ACF would ensure non-attorneys adequately represent the child's tribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory amendment language (§ 1356.60(c)(4) and (c)(2)(xi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed insertion of § 1356.60(c)(4) listing the three categories of allowable legal representation costs and a new § 1356.60(c)(2)(xi) cross-referencing legal representation costs described in paragraph (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory text enumerates (i) agency attorney representation, (ii) independent legal representation for eligible children/parents/relative caregivers including certain civil proceedings and service-linkage activities, and (iii) tribal attorney representation when tribe intervenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and tribal consultation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: ACF frames the NPRM as advancing equity and describes tribal consultation requirements under Executive Order 13175 and ACF policy; ACF states the final rule 'does not meet either standard for consultation' but plans to conduct tribal consultation during the public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains when tribal consultation is triggered (significant direct effects, funding, program delivery, or distribution of power/responsibilities), ACF's interpretation for this NPRM, and the agency's intent to solicit tribal input despite concluding mandatory consultation thresholds are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage between allowable legal representation and specific statutory plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable legal representation is tied to executing specific statutory plan requirements (e.g., reasonable efforts to prevent removal, finalize permanency, educational stability, transition planning, documentation requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF provides statutory citations (sections 471(a), 472(i), 475 subsections, etc.) and concrete examples showing how legal representation supports compliance with particular title IV-E obligations (e.g., paternity to establish eligibility, legal advocacy to secure housing under case plan).
